- |

          echo "Running in normal mode"

items.title: Cross-compilation with podman or docker

milestone.title: Future

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I had too many problems with GitHub action, so I decided to find a way to build windows executable and installer from my Linux box.
To avoid touching my system, I made my own Podman container (that may work with Docker too).

I provide below my Containerfile (you may rename it Dockerfile, but please leave OCI agnostic naming being the default now) and the scripts.

Note that I need `-skipbindings` for Windows at this time, bindings are created with the first build for Linux.

### Describe the solution you'd like

The Containerfile:

```containerfile
FROM fedora:42

RUN set -xe;\
  echo "fastestmirror=true" >> /etc/dnf/dnf.conf;\
  echo "max_parallel_downloads=20" >> /etc/dnf/dnf.conf;\
  echo "deltarpm=1" >> /etc/dnf/dnf.conf;\
  echo "ip_resolve=4" >> /etc/dnf/dnf.conf;\
  dnf install -y golang nodejs mingw64-gcc mingw32-nsiswrapper.noarch mingw-nsis-base.x86_64 upx gtk3-devel webkit2gtk4.0-devel;

RUN set -xe;\
  useradd -m -u 1000 -g 0 -G 0 -s /bin/bash user; \
  usermod -aG wheel user; \
  echo '%wheel ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' >> /etc/sudoers;

USER user
ENV PATH=/home/user/go/bin:$PATH
RUN go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest

USER root
COPY --chmod=755 ./build.sh /usr/local/bin
COPY --chmod=755 ./build-windows.sh /usr/local/bin

USER user
VOLUME /opt/app
WORKDIR /opt/app
```

I prefer Fedora as the tools are well packaged.

The build.sh file:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

go clean -cache -modcache
wails build -upx
```

And the build-windows.sh file:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
export CC=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc GOOS=windows
go clean -cache -modcache
wails build -upx -skipbindings -nsis
```

Now being on my project, I do:

```bas
podman run --userns=keep-id --rm -it -v .:/opt/app:Z wailsbuilder build.sh
podman run --userns=keep-id --rm -it -v .:/opt/app:Z wailsbuilder build-windows.sh
```

All binaries are created. I tried installation on Windows 11 and that works.



### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### Additional context

I use Podman as it allows me to keep the user ID - but docker may work, it only changes the owner of produced binaries. `chown` fixes this.

Do you want me to create a repository, named "wails-cross-builder" for example? So the image may be taken from gcr.io? Or do you want to integrate it into the Wails project (with enhancements of course)

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, wails documentation and convention tells users to put the `wails`/`wails3` tool on their `$PATH`.

There's another way.  The `go tool` command can now be used to run commands using versions from the nearest go module and its sum file.  This offers greater setup simplicity, gives version management "for free", and makes it much easier to work on multiple different Wails projects (potentially at different versions) at once in a reliable and carefree way.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Setting up to be able to use `go tool` is a one-line addition to the `go.mod` file for a project:

```
tool github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3
```

(or, `tool github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails` for v2.)

Then, everywhere that uses `wails3` as a command can instead be `go tool wails3`, and everything works exactly the same... except you're definitely getting the version of the tool that matches with everything else in your go module, and you don't need any additional setup steps to put it onto your `$PATH`.

In Wails v2, this is mostly a user's concern -- they just run `go tool wails dev`, `go tool wails build`, etc etc, in their shell.  (Or wrap a makefile around it to shorten things and offer reminders; potato potato.)

In Wails v3, the tooling invokes itself quite a bit, so this isn't just a matter of how the user holds it.  The Taskfile system invokes `wails3` in several places, and updating all those to `go tool wails3` is necessary to get the desired of result of one-version-across-the-project.  Doing this in a project after it's been templated is possible but a bit of a slog.  All of the changes are in `Taskfile.yml` files or the `build/config.yml` file (but there's a lot of them; I think 17).

I propose in Wails v3, the new project template (e.g. `v3/internal/commands/build_assets/Taskfile.tmpl.yml` and friends) could do this `go tool wails3` pattern out-of-box.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I've been doing this in my Wails projects for a while now and it's great.  I'm not really aware of any downsides at all.


### Additional context

_No response_

### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version v3.0.0-beta.27 ### Operating System Windows ### Description After upgrading a Windows application from Wails v3.0.0-alpha2.117 to v3.0.0-beta.27, the native window appears promptly but its content stays blank noticeably longer. The example imports 24 tiny local ES modules in parallel, then inserts a heading and two paragraphs into the DOM. Each module handler immediately returns a single export statement. On my machine, production builds gave the following FCP timings. Each version has 8 measured launches after one warm-up; execution order alternates between versions. | Version | Median | Range | Launches above 1 second | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | alpha2.117 | 602.9 ms | 582.8–674.0 ms | 0/8 | | beta.27 | 2102.1 ms | 592.6–2676.3 ms | 7/8 | In all 8 beta samples, the DOM insertion finished 96.3–108.6 ms after navigation began. In the slow samples, FCP followed about 1–2 seconds later. No JavaScript long tasks (>50 ms), error events, or unhandled rejections were captured. The two binaries run from the same executable path, use the same WebView2 user-data directory and have the same window size. ### To Reproduce [Wails-Startup-Repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33025737/Wails-Startup-Repro.zip) 1. Extract the archive on Windows with Go 1.25+, PowerShell 7 and WebView2 installed. 2. Open PowerShell in the extracted Wails-Startup-Repro directory and run: ```powershell ./build.ps1 ./profile.ps1 -Runs 8 -Warmups 1 -Modules 24 ``` 3. Compare results/\/summary.json and samples.json. Individual \-\.json files contain the browser paint entries, navigation/resource timing, DOM insertion time, visibility changes, long tasks and errors. environment.json records the environment, build information and hashes. The key frontend sequence is simply: ```js await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: moduleCount }, (_, index) => import(`/modules/${index}.js`))) document.querySelector('#app').innerHTML = '

First content is visible

...' ``` ### Expected behaviour Once the imports have completed and content has been inserted into a visible window, the first contentful paint should follow promptly, without an additional intermittent 1–2 second blank interval. items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The current build pipeline assumes that the entrypoint `main.go` is always in the project root. This is fine for smaller POC projects, however in a larger `go` project, you would normally have a couple of entry points for different builds. 

Some examples are a "Pro" vs a "Community" edition, or an internal dev version with telemetry vs an external version for distribution.

an example structure would be:
```go
<project root>
|-- build
     |-- <build artifacts>
|-- cmd
     |-- server
          |-- main.go   // (server entrypoint)
     |-- desktop-app
          |-- main.go   // (external app entrypoint)
     |-- desktop-app-internal
          |-- main.go   // (internal app entrypoint)
|-- src
     |-- frontend
          |-- <frontend js>
|-- go.mod
|-- go.sum
```


### Describe the solution you'd like

A couple of ways of implementing this would be:
* Add config option to config file
* Add cli option to specify entrypoint (would normally used in conjuction with a `Makefile`)

There are a couple of locations where the entrypoint directory is assumed to be `os.Getwd()`

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/158fd41a8b7d63f8728341716d9b78b6fac20327/v2/pkg/commands/bindings/bindings.go#L39-L41
https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/158fd41a8b7d63f8728341716d9b78b6fac20327/v2/pkg/commands/bindings/bindings.go#L63-L66

### Describe alternatives you've considered

It's possible to eject the app and not utilize the `wails` cli, but you'd have to redefine the entire build pipeline logic which is a bit unnecessary.

### Additional context

This is more of a note for roadmap or anyone who wants to take a stab at a relatively simple `PR`.

_(If I can get some dev time next month, I'll see if I can take a stab at a PR)_

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.28

### Operating System

iOS (experimental)

### Description


Building with `wails3 task ios:run` on a machine that cannot upgrade beyond Xcode 14.2 fails with:

```
application_ios.m:192:24: error: property 'inspectable' not found on object of type 'WKWebView *'
```

The relevant code:

```objc
if (@available(iOS 16.4, *)) {
    vc.webView.inspectable = inspectorOn; // <-- compile error
}
```

**Root cause:** `@available` only guards runtime execution. The compiler still needs to resolve `inspectable` against the iOS SDK headers at **compile time**. Xcode 14.2 ships with an iOS SDK older than 16.4, so the symbol does not exist in the headers, and compilation fails before any runtime check is considered. This is consistent with reports from other projects using Xcode 14.2 with `WKWebView.inspectable`.

**Relevant context:** Apple’s documentation explicitly states that apps linked against an SDK before iOS 16.4 will not have the `inspectable` property available at compile time, and recommends conditional compilation guarded by SDK version macros for this scenario.


### To Reproduce

```bash
go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@latest
wails3 init -n mymob
cd mymob
wails3 task ios:run
```

### Expected behaviour

The project should compile successfully with Xcode 14.2 (iOS SDK < 16.4), or the documentation should clearly state that Xcode 14.3+ is required. Ideally, wails3 task ios:run should complete without errors on Xcode 14.2, using compile-time SDK guards so that WKWebView.inspectable is only referenced when the iOS 16.4 SDK is available.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

## 2. Suggested Conditional Compilation Fix

Replace the direct property access with a compile-time guard:

```objc
#if defined(__IPHONE_16_4) && __IPHONE_OS_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= 160400
    if (@available(iOS 16.4, *)) {
        vc.webView.inspectable = inspectorOn;
    } else
#endif
    {
        @try { [vc.webView setValue:@(inspectorOn) forKey:@"inspectable"]; } @catch (__unused NSException *e) {}
    }
```
**How it works:**
- `__IPHONE_16_4` is only defined when compiling against the iOS 16.4 SDK (Xcode 14.3+).
- `__IPHONE_OS_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED` reflects the SDK’s maximum supported iOS version.
- When using Xcode 14.2, the preprocessor skips the entire `if (@available(...))` block, so the compiler never sees `vc.webView.inspectable`. The KVC fallback (`setValue:forKey:`) still handles runtime behavior on iOS 16.4+ devices.

A simpler alternative that also works: remove the `@available` branch entirely and rely solely on the existing KVC path, since `@"inspectable"` is just a string key and requires no SDK declaration.

### System Details

items.title: [v3] dev readiness check never passes against Vite (no Accept header → 404)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.27

### Operating System

Windows

### Description

Since #6150 (v3.0.0-beta.26), `wails3 dev` adds an HTTP readiness check to the standard
`wails3 task common:dev:frontend` background step. Holding the primary back until the frontend is
reachable is intended, and that part works as designed.

The check itself never succeeds against a Vite dev server. It requests `FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL`
with a bare `http.Client`, which sends **no `Accept` header**. Vite answers a `GET /` without
`Accept` with **404**, while the probe requires exactly **HTTP 200**. The gate therefore blocks
`wails3 task run` for its entire 60s budget and only reports the failure at timeout — so the
symptom is a one-minute hang followed by an error, not a "the frontend is down" message.

Observed on Windows ( first on `v3.0.0-beta.26`, still present on `v3.0.0-beta.27` ):

```
ERROR   starting processes: process "wails3 task common:dev:frontend" did not become ready
on http://localhost:9245 within 1m0s: context deadline exceeded
```

Minimal repro is a stock `wails3 init` project — no project-specific configuration is involved.

### To Reproduce

1. Use any Wails v3 project with a Vite frontend and the default `build/config.yml` `dev_mode`
   block (i.e. `wails3 task common:dev:frontend` as a `background` step, with no explicit
   `readiness` on it).
2. Run `wails3 dev`.
3. Vite starts and is serving correctly:

   ```
   VITE v3.2.11  ready in 474 ms
   ➜  Local:   http://127.0.0.1:9245/
   ```

4. After ~60 seconds:

   ```
   ERROR   starting processes: process "wails3 task common:dev:frontend" did not become ready
   on http://localhost:9245 within 1m0s: context deadline exceeded
   ```

5. The primary process is never launched, and wails3 exit.

Directly showing the mismatch — **same Vite server, same address, only the request headers differ**:

```
default Go http.Client (no Accept)   -> HTTP 404
+ Accept: */*                        -> HTTP 200 (index.html)
+ Accept: text/html                  -> HTTP 200
curl (Accept stripped)               -> HTTP 404
curl (Accept: */*)                   -> HTTP 200
```

### Expected behaviour

The probe should receive HTTP 200 from the healthy frontend dev server within milliseconds and the
primary should start normally. `FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL` points at a server that happily returns
`index.html` for `/` to a browser, so the readiness check should not depend on a header that every
browser sends but Go's default client does not.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

* Searched the issue tracker and discussions for "did not become ready", readiness, and dev-server
  readiness. The nearest matches are unrelated: #6048 (dev teardown), #4905 (connecting to an
  already-running frontend), #4556 (proxy dial to `[::1]`), #4620 (Vite 7.1.8).
* Ruled out an IP/host mismatch, which was the obvious first suspicion:
  * `http://localhost:9245/` and `http://127.0.0.1:9245/` behave identically (both 404 with a bare
    Go client, both 200 with `Accept` sent).
  * This Vite dev server performs no Host check — `Host: evil.com` also returns 200.
* Verified the probe target itself is reachable and fast from Go: with a server bound to
  `127.0.0.1:9245`, `http.Client{Timeout: 100ms}.Get("http://localhost:9245/")` succeeds 10/10 in
  ~1ms, so the 60s budget is not the constraint.
* Isolated the difference to the request headers (table above), which led to the root cause.
* Applied the TCP workaround below, which makes `wails3 dev` work end-to-end — confirming the rest
  of the dev flow is unaffected.

### System Details

```shell

# Diagnosis
 SUCCESS  Your system is ready for Wails development!
```

### Additional context

Go's default `http.Client` sends no `Accept` header, the request reaches Vite without one and
Vite returns 404. `ready` is therefore never true; the loop retries every `interval` (100ms) until the
60s deadline expires, and `runCycle` then returns before it ever reaches the `Primary` step
(`process/process.go:283`).

### Suggested fix

Set an `Accept` header on the readiness request:

```go
req.Header.Set("Accept", "*/*")
```

items.title: `wails doctor` falsely reports `libwebkit  | webkit2gtk4.0-devel` installed on Fedora 41
items.body:
### Description

On Fedora 41, it appears that `wails doctor` falsely reports `webkit2gtk4.0-devel` as installed.

### To Reproduce

On Fedora 41, when I run `wails dev` I see:
```
Package 'webkit2gtk-4.0' not found
```

I ran `wails doctor` and it said `webkit2gtk4.0-devel` was installed.

```
# Dependencies
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
| Dependency | Package Name        | Status    | Version |
| *docker    | moby-engine         | Installed | 28.3.0  |
| gcc        | gcc-c++             | Installed | 14.3.1  |
| libgtk-3   | gtk3-devel          | Installed | 3.24.43 |
| libwebkit  | webkit2gtk4.0-devel | Installed | 2.46.5  |
| npm        | nodejs-npm          | Installed | 10.9.2  |
| pkg-config | pkgconf-pkg-config  | Installed | 2.3.0   |
| *upx       | upx                 | Installed | 5.0.1   |
|                                                        |
└─────────────── * - Optional Dependency ────────────────┘
```

However, after running `sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.0-devel` the error went away and `wails dev` started working.

### Expected behaviour

If `webkit2gtk4.0-devel` is not installed on Fedora 41, `wails doctor` should say it is not installed.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

_No response_

### System Details

```shell

| Dependency | Package Name        | Status    | Version |

| *upx       | upx                 | Installed | 5.0.1   |

```

items.body:
### Wails version family

v3

### Exact Wails version

v3.0.0-beta.1

### Operating System

macOS

### Description

On a MacBook Pro with a 120 Hz ProMotion display, a Wails v3 WKWebView is capped at approximately 60 FPS even though the same WebKit version is capable of rendering at 120 FPS.

Environment:

- macOS 26.5.2 (Build 25F84)
- MacBook Pro with 120 Hz ProMotion display
- macOS SDK 26.5
- Application binary:
  - minos 12.0
  - sdk 26.5

A simple requestAnimationFrame counter consistently reports approximately 60 FPS inside Wails.

Safari also defaults to approximately 60 FPS, but disabling Safari's "Prefer Page Rendering Updates near 60fps" feature flag immediately allows the same test to run at approximately 120 FPS.

More importantly, applying the equivalent WebKit preference directly to the WKWebView created by Wails also immediately changes the Wails application from approximately 60 FPS to approximately 120 FPS.

The preference is:

PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled

I tested this by modifying v3/pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go and disabling the preference through the private WKPreferences feature API immediately after the WKWebView is created.

Before:

requestAnimationFrame ≈ 60 FPS

After disabling PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled:

requestAnimationFrame ≈ 120 FPS

This appears particularly interesting on macOS 26 because the related Tauri investigation reports that the 60 FPS cap no longer applies to WKWebView on Tahoe and that this private preference should effectively be a no-op there.

However, with Wails v3 on macOS 26.5.2, the preference clearly still affects rendering cadence: disabling it changes the WebView from 60 Hz to 120 Hz.

Related investigation:

https://github.com/userFRM/tauri-plugin-macos-fps

Their compatibility notes currently state that on macOS 26 Tahoe, WKWebView runs at native refresh rate without the plugin. That does not appear to be the case for the WKWebView created by Wails v3 on my system.

### To Reproduce

1. Run a Wails v3 application on a MacBook Pro with a 120 Hz ProMotion display.

2. Run this code in the frontend:
```
let frames = 0;
let start = performance.now();

function frame(now) {
    frames++;

    if (now - start >= 1000) {
        console.log(
            (frames * 1000 / (now - start)).toFixed(1),
            "FPS"
        );

        frames = 0;
        start = now;
    }

    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

requestAnimationFrame(frame);
```

3. Observe approximately 60 FPS.

For comparison, in Safari 26 on the same machine:

1. Enable the Develop features.
2. Disable "Prefer Page Rendering Updates near 60fps".
3. Run the same test.
4. Observe approximately 120 FPS.

I then modified Wails' macOS WebView creation code to disable the equivalent private WebKit feature immediately after WKWebView creation.

After rebuilding, the same requestAnimationFrame test reports approximately 120 FPS.

### Expected behaviour

On a 120 Hz ProMotion display, a Wails WKWebView should be capable of receiving rendering updates at the display's native refresh rate rather than being limited to approximately 60 Hz.

Ideally this should work without relying on private WebKit APIs.

I am not necessarily suggesting that Wails should ship the private _features / _setEnabled:forFeature: workaround, since those APIs are undocumented.

The main issue is that Wails' WKWebView appears to remain in WebKit's 60 FPS mode on macOS 26, whereas other investigation suggests that normal WKWebView instances on Tahoe should no longer be capped.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

* Confirmed the MacBook display is running ProMotion.
* Confirmed `requestAnimationFrame` is approximately 60 FPS in Wails.
* Confirmed Safari is initially approximately 60 FPS.
* Disabled Safari's "Prefer Page Rendering Updates near 60fps" feature flag and confirmed Safari immediately reaches approximately 120 FPS.
* Tested loading the Wails frontend over normal `http://localhost` rather than the Wails custom URL scheme. Wails remained at approximately 60 FPS.
* Changed `WKWebViewConfiguration.suppressesIncrementalRendering` from `true` to `false`. No effect; Wails remained approximately 60 FPS.
* Confirmed the application is being built against the macOS 26.5 SDK:

```
cmd LC_BUILD_VERSION
cmdsize 32
platform 1
minos 12.0
sdk 26.5
ntools 1
tool 3
```

* I then modified `v3/pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go` to disable WebKit's private `PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled` feature on the `WKWebView`.

I added:

```
#import <objc/message.h>

static void disableWebKit60FPSCap(WKWebView *webView) {
    WKPreferences *preferences = webView.configuration.preferences;

    Class preferencesClass = NSClassFromString(@"WKPreferences");
    SEL featuresSelector = NSSelectorFromString(@"_features");
    SEL setEnabledSelector = NSSelectorFromString(@"_setEnabled:forFeature:");

    if (preferencesClass == nil ||
        ![preferencesClass respondsToSelector:featuresSelector] ||
        ![preferences respondsToSelector:setEnabledSelector]) {
        return;
    }

    typedef NSArray *(*FeaturesFn)(id, SEL);
    NSArray *features =
        ((FeaturesFn)objc_msgSend)(preferencesClass, featuresSelector);

    for (id feature in features) {
        NSString *key = [feature valueForKey:@"key"];

        if ([key isEqualToString:@"PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled"]) {
            typedef void (*SetEnabledFn)(id, SEL, BOOL, id);

            ((SetEnabledFn)objc_msgSend)(
                preferences,
                setEnabledSelector,
                NO,
                feature
            );

            return;
        }
    }
}
```

and called it immediately after the `WKWebView` is created:

```objc
WKWebView* webView =
    [[WKWebView alloc] initWithFrame:frame configuration:config];

disableWebKit60FPSCap(webView);
```

After rebuilding, the same `requestAnimationFrame` test changed from approximately 60 FPS to approximately 120 FPS.

Removing this patch and rebuilding immediately brings the rendering FPS back to 60.

So the private WebKit preference workaround is confirmed to affect the Wails WebView on macOS 26.5.2.

Its current macOS compatibility documentation reports:

- macOS 13 Ventura: 60 FPS cap exists
- macOS 14 Sonoma: 60 FPS cap exists
- macOS 15 Sequoia: 60 FPS cap exists
- macOS 26 Tahoe: cap removed

It specifically reports testing WKWebView on macOS 26.3.1 with both a 120 Hz ProMotion display and a 165 Hz external display, with both reaching native refresh rate regardless of whether the private preference was changed.

That makes the Wails result unexpected.

On macOS 26.5.2, the Wails v3 WebView remains at approximately 60 FPS, and explicitly disabling PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled still causes it to jump to approximately 120 FPS.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently wails command when launched without any arguments ask for user name and email. It writtes data into:
`/home/user/.wails/wails.json`

Here is full specification if you would like to know more:
https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Maybe wails should be backward compatible for some time and read `~/.wails/wails.json` for some time, but new configs should go into "correct" directory.

items.title: v3 macOS: repeat package and dev restart fail signing bundles in file-provider-backed folders

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
## Problem

On macOS, a Wails v3 project in a file-provider-backed Documents folder packages successfully once, then `wails3 package` fails on the next run at `codesign --force --deep --sign -` with:

```
resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

The same problem prevents the second `wails3 dev` run after a Go source change from restarting its `.dev.app`. `wails3 tool sign` can also report success on this bundle while a subsequent `codesign --verify --deep --strict` fails, because Finder metadata is attached again.

## Reproduction (2026-10-05 master `aab280f2880bc6569f0773af84496c643364436c`)

Host: macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Xcode 26.6, Go 1.26.2. Generate a vanilla or React project under a file-provider-backed `~/Documents` folder.

1. Build the CLI from `v3/cmd/wails3`.
2. `wails3 init -n ReadyReact -t react -d <Documents-folder>`.
3. `cd <Documents-folder>/ReadyReact && wails3 package` — succeeds and creates an ad-hoc signed `.app`.
4. Run `wails3 package` again — fails at `darwin:codesign:adhoc` with the message above.
5. `xattr -lr bin/readyreact.app` shows `com.apple.FinderInfo`, `com.apple.fileprovider.fpfs#P`, and `com.apple.provenance` on the bundle. The failing CLI output is `bin/readyreact.app: replacing existing signature` followed by the error.

With `wails3 dev` in the same folder, editing `main.go` triggers a successful Go rebuild, but `darwin:run` fails while re-signing the existing `.dev.app`; the watcher exits instead of restarting the app.

**Control:** The same CLI and master source generated a React JavaScript project in `/private/tmp`. Two successive `wails3 package` runs both succeeded and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed. A vanilla project there restarted successfully after a Go edit with a new app PID. Direct Developer ID signing of a clean bundle in `/private/tmp` also passed strict verification.

## Expected

Repeated packaging and Go-triggered dev restarts work from common macOS project locations, including file-provider-backed Documents folders. Signing either succeeds with a bundle that passes strict verification or reports the failure clearly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated `wails3 package` on the same macOS project succeeds in a file-provider-backed folder.
- A Go edit during `wails3 dev` restarts the macOS app in that folder.
- Both ad-hoc and Developer ID signed bundles pass `codesign --verify --deep --strict` after the command completes.
- Add a regression check for disallowed bundle extended attributes before re-signing, or document an equivalent robust handling path.

items.title: Loading of 'relative file' linuxdb.yaml results in hardcoded ties to source location

labels.name: awaiting feedback
labels.description: More information is required from the requestor

items.body:
**Description**

The current implementation of LoadRelativeFile() in cmd/fs.go leverages 'runtime.Caller(0)' to form the absolute path to a relative file (runtime.Caller(0) + relativeFile). LoadRelativeFile() appears to solely be used by NewLinuxDB() in cmd/linuxdb.go when loading cmd/linuxdb.yaml. The use of runtime.Caller(0) causes the built binary to reference the source location of where the binary was built when loading './linuxdb.yaml' rather than the location of the executing binary.

Example:
Assume wails source is cloned into '/home/foo/wailsapp/wails' and is built running 'go build/install' in cmd/wails. If the resulting binary is deployed to /usr/local/bin on a system, it attempts to load 'linuxdb.yaml' from '/home/foo/wailsapp/wails/cmd/linuxdb.yaml' when run.

Change where this was originally implemented:
wailsapp/wails@af30e5e6ba8d7763ec07fd726bd0e8e918e99929

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Clone wails source to /home/[user]/wailsapp/wails.
2. Build wails using 'go build/install' from 'cmd/wails'.
3. Copy the resulting wails binary to /usr/local/bin to make it available system wide.
4. Delete /home/[user]/wailsapp.
5. Run /usr/local/bin/wails.

**Expected behaviour**
The resulting binary can be deployed system wide without being tied to the source location where the binary was built. Either linuxdb.yaml is incorporated into the resulting binary or it can be provided along with the binary and loaded as a file relative to the binary.

items.title: [v3][macOS] Back-to-back Window.Close() calls crash in native windowClose (beta.25)

milestone.title: v3.0.0 GA
milestone.description: Wails v3.0.0 General Availability. Track relevant v3 work here. Beta releases are nightly builds and are not planned as separate milestones.

items.body:
### Wails version family v3 ### Exact Wails version `v3.0.0-beta.25` (confirmed with `go run github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-beta.25 version`). Also reproduced on `v3.0.0-beta.20`. The latest-beta reproduction below uses a separate module pinned to beta.25, not a local framework checkout or fork. ### Operating System macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon / arm64. ### Description Two back-to-back frontend `Window.Close()` calls for the same secondary window can terminate the entire application with a SIGSEGV in `_Cfunc_windowClose`. The standalone example below reproduces this without DCV, AWS, custom application cgo, native retain/release workarounds, MCP, window polling, or private macOS API build tags. The main window remains open, so this is not normal application termination after closing the last window. **Observed on beta.25:** the initial run and three additional runs all crashed with the same native close stack (process exit 2). Removing only the second `Window.Close()` call produced a successful control run: the secondary window closed and the main window survived until the example's intentional five-second shutdown. ### To Reproduce 1. Save the following as `main.go` in an empty directory. 2. Run: ```sh go mod init example.com/wails-double-close go get github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3@v3.0.0-beta.25 go mod tidy go build -o repro . ./repro ``` 3. The secondary window automatically requests close twice after one second. The process crashes before printing `SURVIVED five seconds`. 4. Control: remove the second `Window.Close()`, rebuild, and rerun. In my test it printed the survival message and exited normally.
Complete standalone main.go ```go package main import ( "fmt" "net/http" "time" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/events" ) func main() { app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "Double Close Repro", Assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html") if r.URL.Path == "/secondary" { fmt.Fprint(w, `

Closing this window twice in one second.

`) return } fmt.Fprint(w, "

Main window should survive the secondary window closing.

") })}, }) app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{ Name: "main", Title: "Main", URL: "/", Width: 480, Height: 240, }) app.Event.RegisterApplicationEventHook(events.Common.ApplicationStarted, func(*application.ApplicationEvent) { app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{ Name: "secondary", Title: "Secondary", URL: "/secondary", Width: 480, Height: 240, }) go func() { time.Sleep(5 * time.Second) fmt.Println("SURVIVED five seconds") app.Quit() }() }) if err := app.Run(); err != nil { panic(err) } } ```
### Expected behaviour Repeated or overlapping close requests for one window should not crash the process. Once native teardown has started, another request should be safely ignored/coalesced or otherwise rejected without dereferencing an invalid native window. The documented `Close()` / `WindowClosing` API does not state that callers must prevent overlapping calls to avoid a process-level memory fault: https://v3.wails.io/reference/window/#close ### Actual behaviour / sanitized stack excerpt ```text SIGSEGV: segmentation violation signal arrived during cgo execution github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application._Cfunc_windowClose(...) github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.(*macosWebviewWindow).close(...) pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go:1332 github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.webviewWindowImpl.close-fm() github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.InvokeSync.func1() pkg/application/mainthread.go:28 github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application.dispatchOnMainThreadCallback(...) pkg/application/mainthread_darwin.go:53 ``` Local filesystem paths and irrelevant runtime addresses are omitted. ### Attempted Fixes / diagnosis **Application workaround:** process the disconnect notification only once, before requesting window closure: ```js let disconnected = false; function onDisconnect(reason) { if (disconnected) return; disconnected = true; // Existing cleanup, then Window.Close() if the user requested disconnect. } ``` This originally surfaced in a remote-desktop application: the bundled DCV SDK can synchronously notify disconnect twice for one disconnect request when data channels exist. The application incorrectly translated both notifications into a close request. That application-side duplication should be guarded, but the small example above removes the SDK entirely and reproduces the native crash. Earlier A/B checks against an actual remote session: - Both the pre-change application and its subsequent clipboard-change revision crashed on the first disconnect in native `windowClose`. - Adding only the three-line JavaScript once guard passed 20 connect/disconnect/reopen cycles, without any Go/cgo changes or native retention workaround. - These tests did not query or snapshot the closing native window. **Suspected framework race, based on source inspection:** `WebviewWindow.Close()` checks destroyed state before queuing `WindowClosing`. Event handling/listeners are asynchronous; the default close listener separately marks the window destroyed and calls the native close operation. Two requests may pass the initial check and schedule teardown twice. The native close path retains its stored `nsWindow` pointer after closing. This appears consistent with the crash, but I have not used NSZombie instrumentation to prove the Objective-C receiver's lifetime. A potential fix would need to make close initiation/teardown single-shot while preserving the documented cancellable hook semantics. I have not patched the Wails dependency. ### System Details `go run github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-beta.25 doctor` completed successfully. Relevant output: ```text Wails CLI: v3.0.0-beta.25 Go Version: go1.27.1 OS: MacOS 27.0 OS build: 26A428 Platform: darwin Architecture: arm64 Apple Silicon: true CPU: Apple M3 GPU: 10 cores Memory: 16 GB CGO_ENABLED: 1 CGO_CFLAGS: CGO_CPPFLAGS: CGO_CXXFLAGS: CGO_LDFLAGS: GOARM64: v8.0 Xcode CLI: 2418 npm: 11.19.1 macOS signing: Not configured SUCCESS No issues found SUCCESS Your system is ready for Wails development! ``` The beta.25 minimal example was built with **no build tags**. The earlier beta.20 application used `private_mac_apis`; the standalone latest-beta result shows that tag is not required. The linker emitted deployment-target warnings (objects built for macOS 13/27 while linking for 11), but both the crashing example and single-close control built successfully with the same toolchain/settings. ### Additional context - Only macOS runtime behavior has been tested; I am not claiming this crash occurs on Windows or Linux. - Potentially related historical issues: #4353 (pending async callbacks after window close) and #4890 (hide/show native handle crash). This report specifically concerns duplicate close initiation and includes a current-beta standalone reproducer. - A separate diagnostic stress test previously exposed a close-versus-window-query failure in `windowZoomGet`. That is **not** the reproducer or stack reported here.

items.body:
**Description**
I mistakenly used `parcel script.js` as a build command, and waited around 15 minutes before noticing that the command starts a webserver (duh), so I changed it to `parcel build script.js`. That would have been way faster to debug if Wails just forwarded STDOUT & STDERR directly instead of showing that beautiful but unneccessary spinner.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Build a Wails application which doesn't have node_modules yet
2. It will take a long time without any log messages
3. The log messages will show up once "npm install" has completed, and in the wrong order, and not at all if the process is taking indefinitely long for some reason

**Expected behaviour**
The log messages show up at the time they occur.

**Additional context**
In https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/79188c503f9ab4518bf2c303f4ad28016100b1eb/cmd/shell.go#L19 it should just assign os.Stdout/Stderr to cmd's Stdout/Stderr IMO - hiding the output doesn't really make it any more user-friendly.

items.title: Running via `go run` gives exec: "wails3": executable file not found in $PATH
items.body:
### Description

I was hoping to use the go.mod-installed version of Wails in order to keep all developers on the same version of the CLI tool. However, when running it via `go run`, Wails appears to try to use `wails3` out of $PATH, rather than looking at the filepath of its own running executable. This has two problems:

1. It will cause a failure if you attempt to run Wails this way and don't have Wails installed system-wide.
2. If you do have Wails installed system-wide, the parent process will call a different child executable, potentially causing runtime errors or inconsistent behavior.

items.title: Support for initializing a "minimal" application
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The `wails init` command generates user interface components that are not always needed and which, therefore, need to be removed when creating a new application.  By "user interface components" I mean the input, button,  "result" div, and logo.


### Describe the solution you'd like

It might desirable to have flags added that would determine the absence or presence of that code.  The flags could be something like `-m` or `-minimal`.  In other words, if one of these flags were used with the `wails init` command, then only a empty window would appear (initially) when the application is run.  Then the developer could add code without the necessity of removing unused code.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Suppose one is developing a svelte application.  It is possible to remove the Greet function from `app.go` and remove the lines within the script, main, and style sections of `frontend/src/App.svelte`.  The frontend/src/assets/images/logo-universal.png file is also something that might not always be used in an application.


### Additional context

Apparently, the code referred to above might be in the `wails/v2/cmd/wails/internal/commands/initialise/templates/templates/svelte/app.tmpl.go` file and the `wails/v2/cmd/wails/internal/commands/initialise/templates/templates/svelte/frontend/src/App.svelte` file.

To be fair, it should be acknowledged that if this proposal were to be implemented, it should be implemented for all the templates not only svelte and  this could be a time-consuming task.

items.title: [v2] `wails build -platform windows/amd64 -nsis` returns ERROR: cannot build nsis installer - no windows targets

labels.name: Ready For Testing
labels.description: A fix is available and needs testing

items.body:
### Description

In wails `v2.0.0-beta.42`, when compiling wails app for windows with `wails build -platform windows/amd64 -nsis`, instead of generating a windows installer executable, it outputs an `ERROR: cannot build nsis installer - no windows targets`. In `build/bin` folder, `wails build` only produced `app.exe`, and no `app_installer.exe`.

### To Reproduce

1. In macOS (may be irrelevant to the OS) terminal, go to wails app folder
2. Execute command `wails build -platform windows/amd64 -nsis`
3. In the output towards the end, see `ERROR: cannot build nsis installer - no windows targets`

### Expected behaviour

The output should show:

```
Creating NSIS installer
------------------------------
  - Building 'amd64' installer: Done.
```

And `wails build` should produce both `app.exe` and `app_installer.exe`

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

I cloned wails repo locally, and tried to debug wails command. In `v2/cmd/wails/internal/commands/build/build.go` on line 337, when I changed

```go
outputFilename, err := build.Build(buildOptions)
```

to

```go
var err error
outputFilename, err = build.Build(buildOptions)
```

It can successfully generate NSIS installer with `wails build` command.

### System Details

```shell
Wails CLI v2.0.0-beta.42

Scanning system - Please wait (this may take a long time)...Done.

System
------
OS:             MacOS
Version:        12.4
ID:             199506
Go Version:     go1.18.4
Platform:       darwin
Architecture:   arm64

Wails
------

----------                      ------------    ------          -------
xcode command line tools        N/A             Installed       2395
npm                             N/A             Installed       8.1.2

Diagnosis

Your system is ready for Wails development!


If Wails is useful to you or your company, please consider sponsoring the project:
https://github.com/sponsors/leaanthony
```


### Additional context

This bug was introduced in PR #1618 and caused by Go's variable shadowing. In that PR, A block of code including line 337 from `v2/cmd/wails/internal/commands/build/build.go` were moved into a `if !dryRun { ... }` block, and changed its behavior to redeclare `outputFilename` as a local variable within the if block.

items.title: Android: no AAB (App Bundle) packaging tasks — Play Store submission impossible
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The Android Taskfile template only includes APK build tasks (`assembleDebug`, `assembleRelease`). Google Play Store has required Android App Bundles (`.aab`) for all new app submissions since August 2021. Developers who build and test their app with APKs discover at submission time that they can't upload to Play Store.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add four Taskfile tasks mirroring the existing APK pattern:

- `assemble:aab` — debug AAB via `./gradlew bundleDebug`
- `assemble:aab:release` — release AAB via `./gradlew bundleRelease`
- `bundle` — production build + release AAB (single arch, mirrors `package`)
- `bundle:fat` — production build + release AAB (all architectures, mirrors `package:fat`)

The existing Gradle signing config (`ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE`) is reused automatically. APK tasks remain unchanged for local/emulator testing.

~20 lines of Taskfile additions per file. Zero risk to existing functionality.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Documenting the `./gradlew bundleRelease` command in a guide - easy to miss, doesn't match the developer's existing `task package` workflow
- Generating both APK and AAB in the existing `package` task - unnecessary build time for local testing where only APK is needed

### Additional context

AAB uses Google's Play App Signing, so the keystore used at build time is the upload key, not the final signing key. This is worth a comment in the task or docs.

Affects:
- `v3/internal/commands/build_assets/android/Taskfile.yml`
- `v3/examples/android/build/android/Taskfile.yml`
- `v3/examples/mobile/build/android/Taskfile.yml`

```bash
D:\Gitlab\mccl>wails dev

Running frontend DevWatcher command: 'npm run dev' 
Building application for development...

Build error - open D:\Gitlab\mccl\frontend\wailsjs\runtime\package.json: Access is denied.

Watching (sub)/directory: D:\Gitlab\mccl

To develop in the browser and call your bound Go methods from Javascript, navigate to: http://localhost:34115
[Rebuild triggered] files updated 
  - Generating bundle assets: Done. 
  - Compiling application: Done. 

Added new directory to watcher: D:\Gitlab\mccl\frontend\wailsjs\runtime 
INF | Serving assets from frontend DevServer URL: http://localhost:3000/ 
DEB | WebView2 Runtime Version '104.0.1293.47' installed. Minimum version required: 94.0.992.31.
Error: mkdir D:\Gitlab\mccl\frontend\wailsjs\go\main: Access is denied. 
Development mode exited 
DevWatcher command exited!
DevWatcher command killed!


```
# Situation

Under I monitored, I found some strange things.
1. First, I need to run `wails build` to generate two folders `go` `runtime`.
2. Then, run `wails dev`,  at `  - Installing frontend dependencies: ...` , it will delete the `runtime` folder.
3. Then, wails cannot find the `runtime` and report errors.
 
# Resolve
#### I try to give `frontend\wailsjs\runtime\package.json` the r&w permissions.

1. `wails build` to get the `runtime` folder.
2. Used the `windows file properties` to remove `read`.
3. run `chmod 777 frontend/wailsjs/runtime/package.json`
4. run `wails dev`
5. Unfortunately, `frontend\wailsjs\runtime\package.json` still removed.

#### I try to keep the `runtime` folder.

1. run `wails dev`
2. get the `runtime` `go` folders.
3. run `chmod 777 frontend/wailsjs/runtime/package.json` and use the `windows file properties` to remove `read propertie` of `go` and `runtime` between `Executing: wails generate module ` and `Installing frontend dependencies: ...`
4. Then wails will keep building, nothing reported.
5. Then reported `Error: mkdir frontend\wailsjs\go\main: Access is denied. `
6. I found the `go` folder removed.

#### I try to watch the `go` folder.

1. run `wails dev`
2. get the `go` folders.
3. run `chmod 777 frontend/wailsjs/runtime/package.json` and use the `windows file properties` to remove `read propertie` of `go` and `runtime` between `Executing: wails generate module ` and `Installing frontend dependencies: ...`
4. Then, All errors are gone.

It's amazing, isn't it?

But then I edit files,
```bash
[Rebuild triggered] files updated 
  - Generating bundle assets: Done. 
  - Compiling application:  
Build error - open D:\Gitlab\mccl\frontend\wailsjs\runtime\package.json: Access is denied. 
```
I found `runtime` deleted again.

sad...

So I guess this is a question of permissions.

_Originally posted by @Maicarons2022 in https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/issues/1752#issuecomment-1219007533_

items.title: Make Vite Server Timeout Configurable
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The vite server timeout is 10 seconds by default (as set here: https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/ca3e4f6c45dc877c4a7f056c59384828f24fd074/v2/cmd/wails/internal/dev/dev.go#L228). This has caused issues if, for some reason, vite is slow to start (see #3307). In my case, I'm building an app on top of sveltekit and tailwind, and each of those vite plugins take around 8 seconds to start in my environment. This exceeds the 10 second timeout, so I _cannot_ run my app using `wails dev`, even though vite starts a few seconds after this failure.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would really like to be able to configure this 10 second timeout to be whatever I want through either the cli or the `wails.json` file. Also, it might be nice to be explicit about _why_ wails failed to find the Vite server URL (`failed to find Vite server URL: Timed out waiting for Vite to output a URL after x seconds` might be a more descriptive message)

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Could also possibly run the dev server separately as a build step and point wails at it.

### Additional context

Even when I don't add _any_ content to sveltekit or tailwind, just loading both of them via vite is enough to exceed the ten second timeout locally.

### Description

`wails dev` is downgrading wails when running `go mod tidy` (or `go get`? but it's during the output that says running `go mod tidy`), causing compilation to fail.

I think this happens if go.mod is using a newer version than the latest tag (`@latest`), even when the CLI is also built using the same commit that is newer than the latest tag.

### To Reproduce

I am using the latest commit on master because of some recent changes that were merged in that my program relies on.

I cloned wails locally, changed to `v2/cmd/wails` and ran `go install`. I confirmed that `wails doctor` says that the latest commit was built:

```
Wails
------
Version:                v2.1.0
Revision:               928bc75602bb1302ed211d5b08b902c58236192a
Modified:               false
...
```

and then I updated my program's go.mod file to use the same  commit (`go get github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@928...` (or `@master` at the time).

But curiously, I noticed that my go.mod file was being modified to revert the version of wails to v2.1.0. This causes a compile error because my code requires the latest changes.

I suspect this function (or something around here) is culprit:

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/55f76a291bc5ee5c92bdedbc6c05c4f4400b85b3/v2/internal/gomod/gomod.go#L86

### Expected behaviour

`wails dev` can run `go mod tidy` and `go get`, but it shouldn't change go.mod if the CLI and code base match, even if they're not on a tagged release.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

I can work around this temporarily by adding a `replace` to my go.mod that points to my locally-cloned copy of the repo.

(see above)

items.title: [v3]`wails3 generate appimage` looks for GTK3 runtime files on the new GTK4 default (alpha.93)
items.body:
### Description

Since alpha.93, the default CGO build target on Linux is GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6 (the GTK3 path is retained behind `-tags gtk3`, per the alpha.93 changelog). But `wails3 generate appimage` still hard-codes the WebKit2GTK 4.x runtime filenames when packaging, so on a runner that only has the GTK4 toolchain installed, AppImage generation aborts:

```
Processing GTK files. [3/5] 60% | 1m13s
ERROR  Unable to locate all required files: libwebkit2gtkinjectedbundle.so
task: Failed to run task "linux:create:appimage": exit status 1
```

The hardcoded list:

https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/v3.0.0-alpha.93/v3/internal/commands/appimage.go#L142

```go
filesNeeded := []string{"WebKitWebProcess", "WebKitNetworkProcess", "libwebkit2gtkinjectedbundle.so"}
```

No branching on build tag, so even when the binary it's packaging is linked against WebKitGTK 6, the bundler still goes looking for the GTK3 set.

### To Reproduce

1. `go.mod` pinned to `github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3 v3.0.0-alpha.93`, no `-tags gtk3`.
2. On Ubuntu 24.04: `sudo apt install libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev` (no GTK3 dev packages).
3. `go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/cmd/wails3@v3.0.0-alpha.93` — succeeds.
4. `go build ./...` — succeeds, links against GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6.
5. `wails3 generate appimage -binary <APP> -icon <ICON> -desktopfile <FILE> -outputdir <DIR> -builddir <DIR>` — fails as above.

### Expected behaviour

When the binary is built against GTK4 / WebKitGTK 6, the AppImage bundler should pick the matching WebKitGTK 6 runtime files instead of the WebKit2GTK 4.x set — either by checking the build tag, ldd'ing the input binary, or taking a CLI flag.

### Attempted Fixes

Workaround that works today: pin the app build to `-tags gtk3` and put `libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` back on the runner. The changelog calls this the "legacy" path, but pre-alpha.93 it was just "the path", so the takeaway from a downstream perspective is "GTK4 AppImage isn't wired up yet" rather than "GTK3 was deprecated and you missed it".

### Additional context

Hit this when bumping a downstream project from alpha.90 → alpha.93. Same `Taskfile.yml` worked at alpha.90 with `libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` installed; failed at alpha.93 with the GTK4 packages; recovered at alpha.93 with `-tags gtk3` + GTK3 packages. Happy to attach `wails doctor` output from a matching Linux env if useful.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

It's a silly thing...and I'm not sure if this happens to anyone else, but I keep running `npm install <package>`  from the root folder. 

The problem is that it then creates a node_modules folder and a package.json in the root, and it seems like everything worked. And then I realise my mistake and have to go remove them and cd into frontend and redo.

Of course, package.json belongs in the frontend directory. And yes I should just be more careful...but what's the fun in that :)

### Describe the solution you'd like

I was thinking it would be great if there was a `wails install <package>`, that essentially just CDs into frontend and runs `npm install <package>`

I know everything in the wails CLI is currently to do with Go and building etc, so not sure if this is the right place for it. But thought I'd bring it up and see what people think?

I think there's a way to add a package.json to the root folder that says "when npm install is run, do this command first" but I couldn't get it working. Something like a "preinstall" in the scripts section I think :/

items.title: [v3] First-class production server build (parity with desktop Taskfiles)
items.body:
## Summary

Server mode (`-tags server`) has no **production** build path. The generated `build:server` task always builds a **dev-tagged** binary, so deployed headless servers ship with dev-only code, no build hardening, and no parity with the rich desktop build/package tasks. We should make a production server build first-class and consistent with the desktop Taskfiles.

## Current behaviour

In the build-assets template (`v3/internal/commands/build_assets/Taskfile.tmpl.yml`), the desktop tasks (`darwin`/`windows`/`linux` `build` → `build:native`) compute `BUILD_FLAGS` with a full profile matrix:

- **production (default):** `-tags production -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-w -s"`
- **DEV (`DEV=true`):** `-gcflags=all="-l"`, no stripping
- **obfuscated:** `garble` + `-tags wails_obfuscated`
- plus `package`, icons, codesign, etc.

The server task, by contrast, is a single bare line:

```yaml
build:server:
  cmds:
    - go build -tags server {{.BUILD_FLAGS}} -o {{.BIN_DIR}}/{{.APP_NAME}}-server{{exeExt}}
```

`BUILD_FLAGS` defaults to empty and `production` is never added.

## Why this matters

`application_dev.go` is gated `//go:build !production` and `application_server.go` is `//go:build server` — the two tags are **orthogonal and composable**, but because `build:server` omits `production`, every server binary pulls in the `!production` dev code paths (dev logger, dev menu items, dev asset middleware) and skips `-trimpath`/strip.

Measured on a real app (modernc SQLite, no CGO):

| Build | Tags / flags | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `task build:server` (today) | `-tags server` | **39.7 MB** |
| production server | `-tags server,production -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-w -s"` | **25.9 MB** (~35% smaller) |

`-tags server,production` **already compiles cleanly today** — the capability exists in the Go layer; only the build tooling is missing.

## Proposed changes

1. **Taskfile parity (primary).** Give `build:server` the same profile matrix as desktop:
   - production by default: `-tags server,production -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-w -s"`, consistent with `task build` being production for desktop;
   - `DEV=true` for a dev server (`-tags server`, no strip);
   - obfuscation parity (`garble` + `wails_obfuscated`);
   - a `package:server` equivalent (the Docker image is the natural "package").
2. **Dockerfile.server** should build the production server (`-tags server,production` + strip) and `CGO_ENABLED=0` for a clean static binary into distroless.
3. Keep `run:server` as a convenience that builds + runs (DEV by default is reasonable for `run`).

## Thoughts on the API surface

Config is mostly already there: `application.Options.Server` (`ServerOptions{Host, Port, TLS, *Timeouts}`) plus `WAILS_SERVER_HOST` / `WAILS_SERVER_PORT` env overrides. So no new Go config is strictly required.

The "API surface" that needs the change is really the **build/task surface** and the **tag semantics**:

- **Make `server` and `production` compose as a documented, first-class combination** (today it's an undocumented `-tags server,production` that users must discover). Decide whether `build:server` is production-by-default (recommended, mirrors desktop `build`) with `DEV=true` opting into the dev server.
- **Asset/middleware behaviour:** a production server should not run the dev asset middleware. Confirm the `!production` dev asset path is fully excluded when `production` is set, so a production server serves only embedded assets.
- **Optional, smaller:** in server mode the desktop-only options (`Window`, `SystemTray`, `Mac`, …) silently no-op. Consider a lightweight `App.IsServer()`/validation or doc note so users aren't surprised, rather than a new options struct.

Net: the gap is build-system + tag wiring + docs, not new runtime config — a "slight" surface change at most.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `task build:server` produces a stripped, production-tagged binary by default; `DEV=true` produces a dev server.
- [ ] Obfuscated server builds supported, matching desktop.
- [ ] `Dockerfile.server` builds the production server (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, static) into distroless.
- [ ] Production server excludes dev-only code paths/middleware (verified: smaller binary, no dev asset proxy).
- [ ] Docs note the `server`/`production` relationship and `ServerOptions`/env config.

_Filed from a real-world server-mode deployment; happy to open a PR for the Taskfile/Dockerfile template changes if the approach looks right._

items.title: v3, installed from source code under alpha release, got "ERROR   Rel: can't make  relative to <project folder>" due to lack of .git folder
items.body:
### Description

If wails3 is installed from the "source code" packet under v3 alpha release, it will fail to init a project due to lack of ".git" folder (not sure if this is a bug or just a temp phase during development)

### To Reproduce

Windows 10 (but it doesn't look like OS related)

1. Downloaded "source code" from [v3.0.0-alpha.4](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/releases/tag/v3.0.0-alpha.4)
2. Unzip it and install it by following commands:
```
cd <wails_download_folder>\v3\cmd\wails
go install
```
3. Go to any folder where I want to create a new project, create a new project
```
wails3 init -n myfirstapp -t svelte-ts
ERROR   Rel: can't make  relative to <my project folder>\myfirstapp
```

### Expected behaviour

A new project should be able to get initialized

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Attempted Fixes

Use git to grab source code. 
I don't know if this would impact the final release, so raise it up just in case

### System Details

```shell
C:\Telus\Projects>wails3 doctor


          Wails Doctor



# Build Environment
Wails CLI      | v3.0.0-alpha.3
Go Version     | go1.22.0

DefaultGODEBUG | httplaxcontentlength=1,httpmuxgo121=1,tls10server=1,tlsrsakex=1,tlsunsafeekm=1
GOAMD64        | v1
GOARCH         | amd64
GOOS           | windows
vcs            | git
vcs.modified   | false

vcs.time       | 2024-02-07T21:31:58Z

# System
Name              | Windows 10 Home
Version           | 2009 (Build: 19045)
ID                | 22H2
Branding          | Windows 10 Home
Platform          | windows
Architecture      | amd64
Go WebView2Loader | true
NSIS              | Not Installed
WebView2 Version  | 121.0.2277.112
CPU               | Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4200U CPU @ 1.60GHz
GPU 1             | Intel(R) HD Graphics Family (Intel Corporation) - Driver: 20.19.15.4531
Memory            | 8GB

# Diagnosis
 SUCCESS  Your system is ready for Wails development!
```


### Additional context

The reason of this ERROR is that:

In "wails\v3\internal\debug\debug.go", func init() will try to find ".git" directory and use it to set var "LocalModulePath"
```
var LocalModulePath = ""

func init() {
	// Check if .git exists in the relative directory from here: ../../..
	// If it does, we are in a local build
	gitDir := RelativePath("..", "..", "..", ".git")
	if _, err := os.Stat(gitDir); err == nil {
		modulePath := RelativePath("..", "..", "..")
		LocalModulePath, _ = filepath.Abs(modulePath)
	}
}
```

However, if the source code is downloaded from alpha release, or whatever method without using git, there won't be ".git" directory by default, therefore, "os.Stat(gitDir)" will return with err "The system cannot find the file specified." then LocalModulePath will remain empty.

Then in the step under "wails\v3\internal\templates\templates.go" func Install(), `relativePath, err = filepath.Rel(projectDir, debug.LocalModulePath)` will return error
```
// Calculate relative path from project directory to LocalModulePath
var relativePath string
relativePath, err = filepath.Rel(projectDir, debug.LocalModulePath)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
```

items.title: (v3) docs: `docs/` is out of sync with `v3/` source — tracking issue for a full accuracy pass
items.body:
## Problem

A line-by-line audit of the v3 documentation site (all `.mdx`/`.md` under `docs/src/content/docs/`) against the actual `v3/` source tree shows that significant parts of the docs document APIs, CLI flags, file paths, and defaults that no longer match the code. The drift is spread across `reference/`, `features/`, `concepts/`, `guides/`, `contributing/`, `migration/`, and several root pages.

## Examples of what's wrong

- **Types that don't exist:** `*application.Application` (54 references — real type is `*application.App`); `application.WailsEvent` / `application.AppEvent` in event callbacks (real types are `*application.ApplicationEvent`, `*application.WindowEvent`, `*application.CustomEvent`).
- **Methods that don't exist:** `window.Centre()`, `window.SetFocus()`, `window.Destroy()`, `window.SetFullscreen(bool)`, and the whole `OnClose`/`OnDestroy`/`OnFocus`/`OnBlur`/`OnMinimise`/… "convenience listener" family; `app.GetWindowByName`/`ByID`, `app.NewWebviewWindowWithOptions`, `app.SetMenu`, `app.OnWindowCreation`, `app.RunWithContext`, `app.ShowNotification`, `application.Get().EmitEvent`; zero-arg `application.NewContextMenu()`.
- **Wrong manager shape:** `app.Screens`/`app.Windows`/`app.ContextMenus` (plural) → singular; `Screen.Width`/`Height` → `Screen.Size.Width`/`Height`.
- **Wrong dialog API:** package-level `application.InfoDialog()`/`QuestionDialog()`/`OpenFileDialog()`/`SaveFileDialog()` don't exist — real shape is `app.Dialog.*()` + `AddButton(...).OnClick(...)`.
- **Frontend bindings shown in v2 form:** `window.wails.Call(...)`, `window.backend.*`, `window.runtime.*`, `wails.CallByID(...)`. Real bindings are ES modules under `frontend/bindings/<full-Go-path>/...` calling `$Call.ByID(...)` from `/wails/runtime.js`. TS map type is documented as `Map<K, V>`/`Record<K, V>` in places — generator emits `{ [_ in K]?: V }`.
- **CLI flags that don't exist:** `wails3 build -ldflags / -platform / -skipbindings / -skip-package / -package / -verbose`; `wails3 dev -race / -verbose`; the `wails3 signing` subcommand. Real `wails3 build` only takes `--tags`.
- **Wrong paths / defaults:** `build/bin/` (real output is `bin/`); `build/build.json` (doesn't exist — config is `Taskfile.yml` + `build/config.yml`); Vite dev port `34115` (real is `9245`); build tags `dev`/`!dev` (real are `!production`/`production`); `pkg/options/`, `pkg/runtime/`, `pkg/menu/`, `mkdocs-website/` (none of these directories exist); `internal/runtime/webview_window_*.go` (per-OS code is actually in `pkg/application/`).
- **`contributing/` deep-dive pages** describe a generator API (`generator.Collect/Analyse/Render/TypeConverter`), a template API (`templates.Load`/`Template.CopyTo`), a CLI framework (`cobra`), a Linux packager (`fpm`), and runtime files (`internal/runtime/webview_window_*.go`, `pkg/application/RACE.md`) that don't match the actual code (`generator.Generate`, `templates.Install` + `gosod`, `clir`, `nfpm`, files under `pkg/application/`, `v3/TESTING.md`).

## Scope

In scope: all `.mdx`/`.md` under `docs/src/content/docs/` except the two pages listed below.

**Out of scope — needs maintainer decision:**

- ⏭ `docs/src/content/docs/reference/updater.mdx`
- ⏭ `docs/src/content/docs/guides/distribution/auto-updates.mdx`

Both document an updater API (`CreateUpdaterService`, `WithUpdateURL`, frontend `CheckForUpdate`, …) that **does not exist anywhere in `v3/pkg/` or `v3/internal/`**. The decision to ship the feature or mark it as "Planned" is a maintainer call.

## Proposed fix

A single follow-up PR

## Acceptance criteria

- Every Go API claim in `docs/src/content/docs/` resolves to a real symbol in `v3/pkg/` or `v3/internal/`.
- Every CLI flag claim resolves to one registered in `internal/flags/*` and wired in `cmd/wails3/main.go`.
- Every file/dir path claim either exists in the `v3/` tree or is documented as generated output (`frontend/bindings/...`, `bin/...`).



### Self-service

- [x] I'd be willing to address this documentation request myself.

items.title: [v2]An error occurs when creating a new project with a template generated by the Generate Template command
items.body:
**Description**
Using the template generated by the `wails generate template` command to create a new project will cause errors in the generated project file.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:
1. Run `wails generate template wails-template-demo`
2. Run `wails init -n Wails-Demo -t ./wails-template-demo`
3. Run `wails dev`
4. See error

**Expected behaviour**
It is hoped that the steps of the third step can be optimized so that the program can run the build process correctly.

**Screenshots**
This is the file generated after running the `wails dev` command.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28185258/154869357-a3533dce-2021-4baf-adbc-8ded3779ff60.png)
![动画](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/28185258/155225649-3b81cb30-d0d2-4d63-afa1-fbe5e1c61258.gif)


**System Details**
```shell
$ wails doctor
Wails CLI v2.0.0-beta.30


Scanning system - Please wait (this may take a long time)...Done.

System
------
OS:             Windows 10 Pro
Version:        2009 (Build: 19044)
ID:             21H2
Go Version:     go1.17.6
Platform:       windows
Architecture:   amd64

Dependency      Package Name    Status          Version
----------      ------------    ------          -------
WebView2        N/A             Installed       98.0.1108.56
npm             N/A             Installed       8.5.1
*upx            N/A             Available

* - Optional Dependency

Diagnosis
---------
Your system is ready for Wails development!
Optional package(s) installation details:
  - upx : Available at https://upx.github.io/

If Wails is useful to you or your company, please consider sponsoring the project:
https://github.com/sponsors/leaanthony
```

**Additional context**
As to why this error occurs, I'm guessing because running `wails dev` causes the `frontend:install` command in `wails.json` to be run, which is supposed to be in `frontend` directory operation, probably because `wails` does not limit the directory, so this command is run in the project root directory, so unnecessary files (`package-lock.json` and `node_modules` directories) are generated.

There are two suggestions for a solution to this problem:
1. Optimize the `wails dev` and `wails build` commands so that they can correctly identify the directory where the front-end project is located instead of the `package.json` file in all directories. For example, you can set a field to specify the directory where the front-end project is located.
2. The project build script files are uniformly moved to the `scripts` directory in the root directory.

items.title: [v3] Menu.Update() can segfault before the application is running
items.body:
### Description

We were previously running with a fork of Wails that included commit 044756a5cd4d101b0723204916983fd00948ca78 from the `v3-alpha-bugfix/mega-menu-fixes` branch, to prevent crashes if `Menu.Update()` is called before the application enters a running state.

We upgraded our fork to the latest wails and lost this commit. We recommend merging it into mainline.

We also needed this patch for it to build successfully on Linux:

```
diff --git a/v3/pkg/application/menu_linux.go b/v3/pkg/application/menu_linux.go
index ee4bde1ab7b..9ccd737740f 100644
--- a/v3/pkg/application/menu_linux.go
+++ b/v3/pkg/application/menu_linux.go
@@ -20,7 +20,7 @@ func (m *linuxMenu) run() {
 }
 
 func (m *linuxMenu) update() {
-	if m.native == 0 || m.menu == nil {
+	if m.native == nil || m.menu == nil {
 		return // Silently ignore update if menu is not initialized
 	}
 	m.processMenu(m.menu)

```

The following commits also did not merge: 6d09663c1c3dac43d09abee66575c59bfafb1410 (similar to #5234.)

items.title: [v2] support for linux/arm
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I have a some Raspberry Pi 3 Model B devices used in "kiosk mode". Currently running programs made with Electron. I would really like to replace Electron with Wails, but Wails V2 only supports linux/arm64.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like Wails to support linux/arm out of the box.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I was able to make linux/arm compile and work, but my solution is not really nice. I'm not really versed in CGO.

How I made it work:

1. "enabled" the linux/arm platform by adding "linux/arm" to the build command.
```
v2/cmd/wails/internal/commands/build/build.go#L232

// Check platform
validPlatformArch := slicer.String([]string{
	...
	"linux",
	"linux/amd64",
	"linux/arm64",
	"linux/arm", <- here
	...
})
```

This resulted in two errors:

```
../../go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.0.0-beta.36/internal/frontend/desktop/linux/responsewriter.go:87:79: cannot use _Ctype_long(contentLength) (value of type _Ctype_long) as type _Ctype_longlong in variable declaration

../../go/pkg/mod/github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2@v2.0.0-beta.36/internal/frontend/desktop/linux/window.go:867:41: cannot use (_Ctype_ulong)(arraySize) (value of type _Ctype_ulong) as type _Ctype_uint in argument to (_Cfunc_allocFileFilterArray)
```

2. Changed the cast of the contentLength variable in the linux/responsewriter

```
v2/internal/frontend/desktop/linux/responsewriter.go#L87

from: 
C.webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish(rw.req, stream, C.long(contentLength), cMimeType)

to:
C.webkit_uri_scheme_request_finish(rw.req, stream, C.int64_t(contentLength), cMimeType)
```

3. Fixed the types for window/OpenFileDialog

```
v2/internal/frontend/desktop/linux/window.go#L867

from:
data.filters = C.allocFileFilterArray((C.ulong)(arraySize))
filters := (*[1 << 30]*C.struct__GtkFileFilter)(unsafe.Pointer(data.filters))

to:
data.filters = C.allocFileFilterArray((C.uint32_t)(arraySize))
filters := (*[1 << 25]*C.struct__GtkFileFilter)(unsafe.Pointer(data.filters))

```

With these modifications I'm able to work with these older devices, but its quite a hack.

The change in the responsewriter works on linux/amd64 without any problem, but the C.allocFileFilterArray() breaks on the same type problem, but the other way around...

items.title: Support pre-build hook with wails dev & wails build

labels.name: awaiting feedback
labels.description: More information is required from the requestor

labels.name: Ready For Testing
labels.description: A fix is available and needs testing

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The problem is that my team already has built our front-end assets, and we just need to include it in our desktop app (https://github.com/ipfs/ipfs-desktop).

You can see in the README of https://github.com/SgtPooki/ipfs-desktop-wails, that we don't need a front-end command to run at all, but we do need a command to run to *get* our prebuilt frontend (see https://github.com/SgtPooki/ipfs-desktop-wails#run-a-local-version).

Since we need to get these front-end assets between `wails dev` and `wails generate module`, we get errors unless we run an explicit command prior to running `wails`. I believe it would be wise for wails to offer a solution for the multitude of usecases a preBuildHook could support.

### Describe the solution you'd like

`wails.json` already has `postBuildHooks`, I would like to propose `preBuildHooks`. Essentially an agnostic version of "frontend:*" though not necessarily a replacement.

For my issue, I would only need to run `./get-webui.sh` in the preBuildHook:

`wails.json`
```json
...
    "preBuildHooks": {
        "*/*": "./get-webui.sh"
    }
...
```

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The only two solutions I could think of that allow us to fully bundle our webui in the app (obtaining via runtime is not a viable solution) are:
1. require build process to run our `get-webui.sh` shell script prior to running wails command
2. move .get-webui.sh to `./frontend/get-webui.sh` and set `"frontend:build": "bash ./get-webui.sh",` in `wails.json`


### Solution 1
This works, and is okay, but definitely not ideal, requires build cmd to be:
```bash
./get-webui.sh && wails build # or wails dev
```
at least on the first run. 

### Solution 2

This is currently what I'm using as it's the desired DX I want. See https://github.com/SgtPooki/ipfs-desktop-wails/commit/fab24911d05a16ac0852414ad82086149b24404c

but allows us to have a single canonical wails build command: 
```bash
wails build # or wails dev
```

#### Some issues with this solution that others may run into

##### With no `./frontend` folder:

```bash
╰─ ✔ ❯ wails dev -v 2
Wails CLI v2.0.0-beta.38


Executing: go mod tidy -compat=1.17
Executing: wails generate module


ERROR:
main.go:10:12: pattern frontend: no matching files found
```

##### with existing `./frontend/.gitkeep`

```bash
╰─ ✔ ❯ wails dev -v 2
Wails CLI v2.0.0-beta.38


Executing: go mod tidy -compat=1.17
Executing: wails generate module


ERROR:
main.go:10:12: pattern frontend: cannot embed directory frontend: contains no embeddable files

exit status 1

If Wails is useful to you or your company, please consider sponsoring the project:
https://github.com/sponsors/leaanthony


exit status 1
```

##### With empty `./frontend/index.html`

This allows things to work, but I don't like the idea that wails could be modifying/hooking into a file that will be overwritten. 

### Additional context

_No response_

items.title: Add Documentation for use with `go build`
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently all the documentation focuses on `wails build`, which is great if that happens to work well with your workflow, and not so great if it doesn't. 

From scanning the debug output of `wails build` I was able to figure out how to build it directly with `go build`, so it's perfectible feasible it would seem. I'm a little confused why you opted for your own build system, at the very least you should cover the build system that your audience is already familiar with.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Cover `go build` use-cases. For example it's not evident how to debug a wails app without using the `wails build` command.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

None. Using `wails build` simply isn't viable for our use-case.

items.title: Cannot set size of window on Ubuntu 22.04 (heigh and width is 0)

labels.name: WIP
labels.description: The issue is currently under development

items.body:
### Description

When running wails, both in dev and build mode on Ubuntu, the height and width are zero. I ran the same exact code on MacOS and it works. 

It's stuck at (seemingly) 0 width and 0 height. If you pass it the `Fullscreen` argument in app initialization, or call `runtime.WindowFullscreen(ctx)` from go, you still start off with 0 widht and 0 height, but it becomes resizable via the GUI.

OS Version:

```
Distributor ID:	Ubuntu
Description:	Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
Release:	22.04
Codename:	jammy
```

Run `wails dev` or run `wails build` and execute build executable
